records.source: וְהִנֵּ֣ה׀אִ֣ישׁ אֱלֹהִ֗ים בָּ֧א מִיהוּדָ֛ה בִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־בֵּֽית־אֵ֑ל וְיָרָבְעָ֛ם עֹמֵ֥ד עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ לְהַקְטִֽיר׃
records.gloss: And look, [a] man of God came from Judah by [the] word of Yahweh to Bethel, and Jeroboam [was] standing by the altar to make smoke.
pieces: Just then a man of God came from Judah to Bethel by the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, while Jeroboam was standing by the altar to burn incense.

L.1: And look, a man of God came from Judah by [the] word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to Bethel, while Jeroboam [was] standing by the altar to burn incense.

R.1: Just then a man of God came from Judah to Bethel. He came at {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s command. Jeroboam was standing by the altar, ready to burn incense.

decisions.choice: a man of God: a prophet, here not named
decisions.reason: "Man of God" is a title for a prophet who speaks for God (1 Samuel 2:27; 9:6). This one is never named. In this chapter he is called "the man of God" throughout, while the man from Bethel in verse 11 is called "the prophet".

decisions.choice: by the word of the LORD: sent by Yahweh's command and acting on it
decisions.reason: The phrase runs through the whole chapter (verses 1, 2, 5, 9, 17, 18, 32). The man of God comes, speaks and is given his instructions by Yahweh's word, and the story turns on whether he will keep to that word when another voice claims it too.

decisions.choice: Jeroboam at his altar: the feast he set up at Bethel (12:32-33)
decisions.reason: Jeroboam had built an altar at Bethel and made a feast of his own choosing in the eighth month, going up to the altar himself to burn offerings (12:32-33). The man of God arrives at that very moment.

decisions.choice: to burn incense, or to make offerings go up in smoke
decisions.reason: The verb means to send something up in smoke on an altar. It is used of incense and also of the fat of sacrifices. Either fits here.

decisions.choice: by the word of the LORD (Literal, Balanced); at the LORD's command (Readable)
decisions.reason: The phrase is kept the same every time it comes back in this chapter, so the reader can follow it. Readable says "at the LORD's command" each time, which is the sense in plain words.

decisions.choice: Just then
decisions.reason: "Look" draws attention to a sudden arrival. Balanced and Readable say "Just then".

records.heading: A man of God from Judah

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֤א עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ בִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ מִזְבֵּ֣חַ מִזְבֵּ֔חַ כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה הִנֵּֽה־בֵ֞ן נוֹלָ֤ד לְבֵית־דָּוִד֙ יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ שְׁמ֔וֹ וְזָבַ֣ח עָלֶ֗יךָ אֶת־כֹּהֲנֵ֤י הַבָּמוֹת֙ הַמַּקְטִרִ֣ים עָלֶ֔יךָ וְעַצְמ֥וֹת אָדָ֖ם יִשְׂרְפ֥וּ עָלֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And he called out against the altar by [the] word of Yahweh and said, Altar, altar, thus says Yahweh: look, a son [will be] born to [the] house of David, Josiah [is] his name, and he will sacrifice on you the priests of the high places who make smoke on you, and bones of man they will burn on you.
pieces: By the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} he cried out against the altar, "Altar, altar! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: 'A son will be born to the house of David, and his name will be Josiah. He will sacrifice on you the priests of the high places who burn their incense here, and human bones will be burned on you.'"

L.2: And he called out against the altar by [the] word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and said, "Altar, altar, thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: 'Look, a son will be born to the house of David, Josiah [is] his name; and he will sacrifice on you the priests of the high places who burn incense on you, and human bones they will burn on you.'"

R.2: At {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s command, he shouted at the altar, "Altar, altar! This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: 'One day David's family will have a son named Josiah. He will kill the priests of the hilltop shrines who burn incense on you, and offer them on you as sacrifices. Human bones will be burned on you.'"

decisions.choice: Josiah: the king of Judah who carried this out (2 Kings 23:15-18)
decisions.reason: About three hundred years later Josiah king of Judah tore down the altar at Bethel. He took bones from the tombs there and burned them on the altar to make it unclean, and he left alone the tomb of the man of God who had foretold it (2 Kings 23:15-18). On the altars of the towns of Samaria he killed the priests of the high places (2 Kings 23:20). Naming a king generations before his birth is rare in Scripture; compare Cyrus in Isaiah 44:28-45:1.

decisions.choice: Altar, altar: the prophecy is spoken to the altar itself
decisions.reason: He does not speak to the king but to the altar, calling it twice for weight. The altar Jeroboam had made stands for the worship he had set up (12:28-33).

decisions.choice: sacrificing priests and burning bones on the altar: making it unclean for ever
decisions.reason: A dead body made anything it touched unclean (Numbers 19:11-16). Killing the priests on their own altar and burning human bones there would defile the altar so that it could never be used again.

decisions.choice: the house of David: the royal family of Judah
decisions.reason: Jeroboam had led the northern tribes away from David's family (12:16-20) and feared they would go back to it (12:26-27). The prophecy says a king from that same family will one day judge this altar.

decisions.choice: the man of God's words in double quotation marks, the LORD's words inside them in single marks
decisions.reason: The man of God speaks, and what he speaks is the LORD's message. Literal says "thus says the LORD", Balanced "The LORD says this" and Readable "This is what the LORD says", as throughout Samuel and Kings.

decisions.choice: kill the priests ... and offer them on you as sacrifices
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "sacrifice the priests" means: they will be killed on the altar like animals offered there.

records.source: וְנָתַן֩ בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֤וּא מוֹפֵת֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר זֶ֣ה הַמּוֹפֵ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה הִנֵּ֤ה הַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ נִקְרָ֔ע וְנִשְׁפַּ֖ךְ הַדֶּ֥שֶׁן אֲשֶׁר־עָלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And he gave on that day a sign, saying, This [is] the sign that spoke Yahweh: look, the altar [will be] torn apart, and poured out the fat-ash which [is] on it.
pieces: That same day he gave a sign: "This is the sign that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken: The altar will be split apart, and the ashes on it will be poured out."

L.3: And he gave a sign on that day, saying, "This [is] the sign that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken: look, the altar will be torn apart, and the ash that [is] on it will be poured out."

R.3: That same day the man of God also gave a sign to show that his message was true. He said, "This is the sign {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given: This altar will split apart, and the ashes on it will spill out."

decisions.choice: sign: a wonder that proves a message true
decisions.reason: The word is used of wonders that show a messenger is sent by God (Exodus 7:9; Deuteronomy 13:2). The far-off prophecy about Josiah is backed by a sign that happens at once (verse 5).

decisions.choice: the ash: the fat-soaked ashes of the offerings
decisions.reason: The word means ashes mixed with the fat of burnt sacrifices, which were removed carefully to a clean place (Leviticus 1:16; 6:3-4). Spilled on the ground, they show the altar's offerings rejected.

decisions.choice: he gave: the man of God gave the sign
decisions.reason: The subject carries on from verse 2. The sign is part of what he announced that day.

decisions.choice: the man of God ... to show that his message was true
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker and says what a sign is for.

records.source: וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶת־דְּבַ֣ר אִישׁ־הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר קָרָ֤א עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ בְּבֵֽית־אֵ֔ל וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח יָרָבְעָ֧ם אֶת־יָד֛וֹ מֵעַ֥ל הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ לֵאמֹ֣ר׀תִּפְשֻׂ֑הוּ וַתִּיבַ֤שׁ יָדוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁלַ֣ח עָלָ֔יו וְלֹ֥א יָכֹ֖ל לַהֲשִׁיבָ֥הּ אֵלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And it was, when heard the king the word of the man of God which he called out against the altar in Bethel, and stretched out Jeroboam his hand from on the altar, saying, Seize him; and dried up his hand which he stretched out against him, and not he was able to bring it back to himself.
pieces: When King Jeroboam heard what the man of God had cried out against the altar at Bethel, he stretched out his hand from the altar and said, "Seize him!" But the hand he had stretched out against him withered, so that he could not pull it back.

L.4: And it happened, when the king heard the word of the man of God that he called out against the altar in Bethel, Jeroboam stretched out his hand from the altar, saying, "Seize him!" And his hand that he stretched out against him dried up, and he was not able to draw it back to himself.

R.4: King Jeroboam heard what the man of God had shouted against the altar at Bethel. He stretched out his hand from the altar toward the man and said, "Grab him!" But the king's hand shriveled up, and he could not pull it back.

decisions.choice: dried up: became stiff and useless
decisions.reason: The verb is used of grass and plants drying out. Here the king's arm became rigid and could not move, so he could not draw it back.

decisions.choice: the hand raised against God's messenger is struck
decisions.reason: The king stretches out his hand as a command to arrest the man of God, and that hand is the one that fails. Yahweh protects the one who speaks his word.

decisions.choice: from the altar: from where he stood beside it
decisions.reason: Jeroboam was standing at the altar (verse 1), probably on its raised platform, and gave the order from there.

decisions.choice: King Jeroboam
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the king" first and names Jeroboam later in the sentence. Balanced and Readable join the two at the start.

records.source: וְהַמִּזְבֵּ֣חַ נִקְרָ֔ע וַיִּשָּׁפֵ֥ךְ הַדֶּ֖שֶׁן מִן־הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ כַּמּוֹפֵ֗ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֛ן אִ֥ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים בִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And the altar was torn apart, and poured out was the fat-ash from the altar, according to the sign which gave the man of God by [the] word of Yahweh.
pieces: The altar was split apart, and the ashes poured out from the altar, in keeping with the sign that the man of God, by the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, had given.

L.5: And the altar was torn apart, and the ash was poured out from the altar, according to the sign that the man of God had given by [the] word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.5: Then the altar split apart, and the ashes spilled out of it. This was the sign the man of God had given at {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s command.

decisions.choice: the altar split: the sign happened at once
decisions.reason: The narrator reports the sign coming true straight away, while the king stands there with his hand stiff. It may have happened in the same moment as verse 4.

decisions.choice: the sign fulfilled confirms the word
decisions.reason: A prophet whose word comes true is shown to be sent by Yahweh (Deuteronomy 18:21-22). The split altar is a pledge that the prophecy about Josiah will also come true.

decisions.choice: This was the sign ...
decisions.reason: Readable makes the last phrase a sentence of its own.

records.source: וַיַּ֨עַן הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀אֶל־אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים חַל־נָ֞א אֶת־פְּנֵ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ וְהִתְפַּלֵּ֣ל בַּעֲדִ֔י וְתָשֹׁ֥ב יָדִ֖י אֵלָ֑י וַיְחַ֤ל אִישׁ־הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַתָּ֤שָׁב יַד־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֵלָ֔יו וַתְּהִ֖י כְּבָרִֽאשֹׁנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And answered the king and said to the man of God, Soften please [the] face of Yahweh your God and pray for me, and may return my hand to me. And softened the man of God [the] face of Yahweh, and returned [the] hand of the king to him, and it was as at the first.
pieces: Then the king said to the man of God, "Please plead with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and pray for me, so that my hand may be restored to me." So the man of God pleaded with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the king's hand was restored to him and became as it was before.

L.6: And the king answered and said to the man of God, "Please soften the face of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and pray for me, so that my hand may come back to me." And the man of God softened the face of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the king's hand came back to him and was as [it was] at the first.

R.6: Then the king said to the man of God, "Please beg {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God to be kind to me, and pray for me, so that my hand will be healed." So the man of God begged {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the king's hand was healed. It was just as it had been before.

decisions.choice: soften the face of the LORD: plead with Yahweh for favor
decisions.reason: The idiom pictures making someone's face pleasant toward you. It is used of earnest prayer that turns away anger (Exodus 32:11; 2 Kings 13:4).

decisions.choice: your God: the king speaks of the LORD as the prophet's God
decisions.reason: Jeroboam asks the man of God to pray to "your God". The wording sets the king at a distance from the God whose altar law he has broken.

decisions.choice: the man of God prays for the king, and the hand is healed
decisions.reason: The one the king tried to seize now prays for him, and Yahweh hears. The healing shows that the power to strike and to restore lies with Yahweh and his word.

decisions.choice: beg the LORD your God to be kind to me; healed
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom of the face and says "healed" for the hand coming back.

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֶל־אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים בֹּאָה־אִתִּ֥י הַבַּ֖יְתָה וּֽסְעָ֑דָה וְאֶתְּנָ֥ה לְךָ֖ מַתָּֽת׃
records.gloss: And spoke the king to the man of God, Come with me home, and refresh yourself, and I will give to you a gift.
pieces: Then the king said to the man of God, "Come to the palace with me and have something to eat, and I will give you a gift."

L.7: And the king spoke to the man of God, "Come with me to the house and refresh yourself, and I will give you a gift."

R.7: The king told the man of God, "Come to my house with me and eat something. I will give you a present."

decisions.choice: refresh yourself: take food to restore your strength
decisions.reason: The verb means to support or sustain, and with food it means a meal that gives strength (Genesis 18:5; Judges 19:5).

decisions.choice: a meal and a gift from the king: a sign of fellowship and favor
decisions.reason: Gifts to prophets were common (1 Samuel 9:7-8; 2 Kings 5:15-16). To eat at the king's table and take his gift would bind the man of God to the king and seem to approve his altar.

decisions.choice: have something to eat
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what "refresh yourself" means here.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אִישׁ־הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אִם־תִּתֶּן־לִי֙ אֶת־חֲצִ֣י בֵיתֶ֔ךָ לֹ֥א אָבֹ֖א עִמָּ֑ךְ וְלֹֽא־אֹ֤כַל לֶ֨חֶם֙ וְלֹ֣א אֶשְׁתֶּה־מַּ֔יִם בַּמָּק֖וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And said the man of God to the king, If you give to me half your house, not I will go with you, and not I will eat bread and not I will drink water in the place the this.
pieces: But the man of God answered the king, "Even if you gave me half your palace, I would not go in with you, and I will not eat bread or drink water in this place.

L.8: And the man of God said to the king, "If you give me half your house, I will not go with you, and I will not eat bread and I will not drink water in this place.

R.8: But the man of God answered the king, "Even if you gave me half of everything you own, I would not go with you. And I will not eat or drink anything in this place.

decisions.choice: half your house: half the king's palace and all it holds
decisions.reason: "House" means the household and its wealth. The point is that no gift could be large enough.

decisions.choice: eat bread and drink water: take any meal at all
decisions.reason: Bread and water stand for food and drink of any kind.

decisions.choice: If you give: even if you were to give
decisions.reason: The condition is not a bargain but a way of saying "never".

decisions.choice: the speech stays open
decisions.reason: The man of God's words go on into verse 9, so the quotation mark closes there.

decisions.choice: half of everything you own
decisions.reason: Readable says what "half your house" stands for.

records.source: כִּֽי־כֵ֣ן׀צִוָּ֣ה אֹתִ֗י בִּדְבַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹא־תֹ֥אכַל לֶ֖חֶם וְלֹ֣א תִשְׁתֶּה־מָּ֑יִם וְלֹ֣א תָשׁ֔וּב בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָלָֽכְתָּ׃
records.gloss: For thus he commanded me by [the] word of Yahweh, saying, Not you shall eat bread and not you shall drink water, and not you shall return by the way which you went.
pieces: For this is the command I was given by the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: 'Eat no bread and drink no water, and do not go back by the way you came.'"

L.9: For thus {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commanded me by [the] word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying, 'You shall not eat bread and you shall not drink water, and you shall not return by the way that you went.'"

R.9: For I was given this order at {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s command: 'Do not eat any food or drink any water. And do not go home by the same road you came on.'"

decisions.choice: he commanded me: Yahweh gave the command through his word
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject, and "by the word of the LORD" shows who gave it. It can also be read as "so I was commanded".

decisions.choice: no eating, no drinking, no going back the same way
decisions.reason: The text does not explain the command. It fits the message he carried: Bethel's worship was rejected, and the man of God was not to share a meal there as a sign of fellowship. Going home by another road may show that he was not to retrace his steps or be found again.

decisions.choice: the command I was given (Balanced); I was given this order (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the verb around so that the reader does not stop to ask who "he" is; the LORD is named in the same sentence.

records.source: וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ אַחֵ֑ר וְלֹֽא־שָׁ֣ב בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֛ר בָּ֥א בָ֖הּ אֶל־בֵּֽית־אֵֽל׃פ
records.gloss: And he went by another way, and not he returned by the way which he came by it to Bethel.
pieces: So he went another way and did not return by the road on which he had come to Bethel.

L.10: And he went by another way, and did not return by the way by which he had come to Bethel.

R.10: So he left by a different road. He did not go back the way he had come to Bethel.

decisions.choice: way: both the road taken and a way of life
decisions.reason: "Way" is a key word in this chapter: the road the man of God must not take back (verses 9, 10, 17), the road the old prophet asks about (verse 12), the road where the lion meets him (verse 24), and Jeroboam's evil way (verse 33).

decisions.choice: he did not return: so far he obeys
decisions.reason: The verb "return" is the one used in the command of verse 9. At this point he keeps it.

decisions.choice: road (Balanced, Readable); way (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "road" where the actual route is meant.

records.source: וְנָבִ֤יא אֶחָד֙ זָקֵ֔ן יֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּבֵֽית־אֵ֑ל וַיָּב֣וֹא בְנ֡וֹ וַיְסַפֶּר־ל֣וֹ אֶת־כָּל־הַמַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂה֩ אִישׁ־הָאֱלֹהִ֨ים׀הַיּ֜וֹם בְּבֵֽית־אֵ֗ל אֶת־הַדְּבָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר אֶל־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַֽיְסַפְּר֖וּם לַאֲבִיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And [a] prophet, one, old, [was] dwelling in Bethel; and came his son and recounted to him all the deed which did the man of God the day in Bethel, the words which he spoke to the king, and they recounted them to their father.
pieces: Now an old prophet was living in Bethel. One of his sons came and told him everything the man of God had done in Bethel that day. His sons also told their father the words he had spoken to the king.

L.11: And a certain old prophet was living in Bethel, and his son came and told him every deed that the man of God had done that day in Bethel; the words that he had spoken to the king, they told them to their father.

R.11: Now an old prophet lived in Bethel. One of his sons came and told him everything the man of God had done in Bethel that day. The sons also told their father what the man of God had said to the king.

decisions.choice: his son came ... they told: one son, then the sons together
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has "his son" with a singular verb, then "they told" with a plural verb, and verses 12-13 speak of "his sons". The ancient Greek, Syriac and Latin translations have "his sons" at the start too. The Hebrew can be read as one son arriving first, with his brothers joining in the telling.

decisions.choice: an old prophet living in Bethel: a prophet of the northern kingdom
decisions.reason: He is called "the prophet" throughout, as the man from Judah is called "the man of God". The text does not say what he thought of Jeroboam's altar. Verses 20-22 show that Yahweh did speak through him.

decisions.choice: that day: the same day as the events at the altar
decisions.reason: The old prophet hears the news while the man of God is still on the road home.

decisions.choice: One of his sons ... His sons also told
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make sense of the change from one son to several, keeping the Hebrew's singular at the start.

records.heading: The old prophet of Bethel

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר אֲלֵהֶם֙ אֲבִיהֶ֔ם אֵֽי־זֶ֥ה הַדֶּ֖רֶךְ הָלָ֑ךְ וַיִּרְא֣וּ בָנָ֗יו אֶת־הַדֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הָלַךְ֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֖א מִיהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And spoke to them their father, Which this way he went? And had seen his sons the way which went the man of God who came from Judah.
pieces: Their father asked them, "Which way did he go?" His sons had seen which road the man of God from Judah had taken.

L.12: And their father said to them, "Which way [is] it that he went?" And his sons had seen the way that the man of God who came from Judah had gone.

R.12: Their father asked them, "Which way did he go?" His sons had seen which road the man of God from Judah had taken.

decisions.choice: his sons had seen: they knew the road
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "and his sons had seen". The ancient Greek and some other translations read "and his sons showed him", which in Hebrew differs only by the vowels and one small form of the verb. The sense is the same: the sons could point out the road.

decisions.choice: which way: the old prophet means to follow him
decisions.reason: The question shows his plan at once; verse 13 carries it out.

decisions.choice: road
decisions.reason: As in verse 10, Balanced and Readable say "road" for the route taken.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־בָּנָ֔יו חִבְשׁוּ־לִ֖י הַחֲמ֑וֹר וַיַּחְבְּשׁוּ־ל֣וֹ הַחֲמ֔וֹר וַיִּרְכַּ֖ב עָלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And he said to his sons, Saddle for me the donkey; and they saddled for him the donkey, and he rode on it.
pieces: "Saddle the donkey for me," he told his sons. They saddled it for him, and he mounted and rode off.

L.13: And he said to his sons, "Saddle the donkey for me." And they saddled the donkey for him, and he rode on it.

R.13: So he said to his sons, "Get the donkey ready for me to ride." They saddled the donkey for him, and he rode away on it.

decisions.choice: the donkey: the usual animal for a journey
decisions.reason: Saddling a donkey is the ordinary way to set out on a trip (Numbers 22:21; 2 Samuel 17:23). The donkey has a part to play later in the story (verses 23-29).

decisions.choice: Get the donkey ready for me to ride
decisions.reason: Readable explains what saddling the donkey was for.

records.source: וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ אַֽחֲרֵי֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיִּ֨מְצָאֵ֔הוּ יֹשֵׁ֖ב תַּ֣חַת הָאֵלָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו הַאַתָּ֧ה אִישׁ־הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֥אתָ מִֽיהוּדָ֖ה וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אָֽנִי׃
records.gloss: And he went after the man of God and found him sitting under the terebinth, and he said to him, [Are] you the man of God who came from Judah? And he said, I.
pieces: He followed the man of God and found him sitting under the terebinth. He asked him, "Are you the man of God who came from Judah?" "I am," he replied.

L.14: And he went after the man of God and found him sitting under the terebinth. And he said to him, "[Are] you the man of God who came from Judah?" And he said, "I [am]."

R.14: He followed the man of God and found him sitting under a big tree. He asked him, "Are you the man of God who came from Judah?" "Yes, I am," the man answered.

decisions.choice: the terebinth: a large shade tree
decisions.reason: The word names a large, spreading tree, sometimes taken as an oak. The Hebrew says "the terebinth", perhaps a tree that was known as a landmark.

decisions.choice: sitting: he has stopped on his way home
decisions.reason: He has not gone back, but he has not yet left the area either. The text records it without comment.

decisions.choice: a big tree
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain description in place of the tree's name.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו לֵ֥ךְ אִתִּ֖י הַבָּ֑יְתָה וֶאֱכֹ֖ל לָֽחֶם׃
records.gloss: And he said to him, Come with me the house, and eat bread.
pieces: Then he said to him, "Come home with me and eat a meal."

L.15: And he said to him, "Come with me to the house and eat bread."

R.15: The old prophet said to him, "Come home with me and have something to eat."

decisions.choice: eat bread: have a meal
decisions.reason: "Bread" stands for food in general. The invitation repeats the king's (verse 7).

decisions.choice: The old prophet
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

records.source: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לֹ֥א אוּכַ֛ל לָשׁ֥וּב אִתָּ֖ךְ וְלָב֣וֹא אִתָּ֑ךְ וְלֹֽא־אֹ֣כַל לֶ֗חֶם וְלֹֽא־אֶשְׁתֶּ֤ה אִתְּךָ֙ מַ֔יִם בַּמָּק֖וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And he said, Not I am able to return with you and to go with you, and not I will eat bread and not I will drink with you water in the place the this.
pieces: He replied, "I cannot turn back with you or go home with you, and I will not eat bread or drink water with you here in this place.

L.16: And he said, "I am not able to return with you or to go with you; and I will not eat bread and I will not drink water with you in this place.

R.16: But the man of God said, "I cannot go back with you or go into your home. And I will not eat or drink anything with you in this place.

decisions.choice: I am not able: I am not allowed
decisions.reason: He is able to walk back; what he means is that the command forbids it.

decisions.choice: return: the forbidden word of verse 9
decisions.reason: "Return" is the very verb of the command. He repeats the command almost word for word to explain himself.

decisions.choice: the speech stays open
decisions.reason: His words continue into verse 17, where the quotation mark closes.

records.source: כִּֽי־דָבָ֤ר אֵלַי֙ בִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה לֹֽא־תֹאכַ֣ל לֶ֔חֶם וְלֹֽא־תִשְׁתֶּ֥ה שָׁ֖ם מָ֑יִם לֹא־תָשׁ֣וּב לָלֶ֔כֶת בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־הָלַ֥כְתָּ בָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: For [a] word [was] to me by [the] word of Yahweh: Not you shall eat bread and not you shall drink there water; not you shall return to go by the way which you went by it.
pieces: For a word came to me by the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: 'Eat no bread and drink no water there, and do not go back by the way you came.'"

L.17: For a word [came] to me by [the] word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: 'You shall not eat bread and you shall not drink water there; you shall not go back by the way by which you went.'"

R.17: For I was given this order at {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s command: 'Do not eat any food or drink any water there. And do not go home by the same road you came on.'"

decisions.choice: a word came to me by the word of the LORD
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is compressed: "a word to me by the word of the LORD". It means he received a direct command from Yahweh.

decisions.choice: the command repeated a third time
decisions.reason: The command is given in verse 9 and repeated here, and the old prophet will repeat it again in verse 22. The repetition makes clear that the man of God knew exactly what he had been told.

decisions.choice: I was given this order at the LORD's command
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the same wording as verse 9.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ גַּם־אֲנִ֣י נָבִיא֮ כָּמוֹךָ֒ וּמַלְאָ֡ךְ דִּבֶּ֣ר אֵלַי֩ בִּדְבַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר הֲשִׁבֵ֤הוּ אִתְּךָ֙ אֶל־בֵּיתֶ֔ךָ וְיֹ֥אכַל לֶ֖חֶם וְיֵ֣שְׁתְּ מָ֑יִם כִּחֵ֖שׁ לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And he said to him, Also I [am a] prophet like you, and [an] angel spoke to me by [the] word of Yahweh, saying, Bring him back with you to your house, and let him eat bread and let him drink water. He lied to him.
pieces: The old prophet said to him, "I am a prophet as well, just as you are, and by the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} an angel told me, 'Bring him back with you to your house so that he can eat bread and drink water.'" But he was lying to him.

L.18: And he said to him, "I also [am] a prophet like you, and an angel spoke to me by [the] word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying, 'Bring him back with you to your house, so that he may eat bread and drink water.'" He lied to him.

R.18: Then the old prophet said, "I am a prophet too, just like you. An angel spoke to me at {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s command. The angel said, 'Bring him back to your house so he can have some food and water.'" But the old prophet was lying to him.

decisions.choice: he lied to him: the claim of a new message was false
decisions.reason: The narrator says it plainly, in two Hebrew words placed after the speech, so the reader knows what the man of God does not. Yahweh had not changed the command. The man of God had heard it from Yahweh himself, and a second-hand claim from another prophet should not have outweighed it; Deuteronomy 13:2-4 warns that even a prophet's word must be tested against what Yahweh has already said. The text gives no reason for the lie: it may have been a test, a wish to have the man of God's honor in his house, or a way to blunt his word against Bethel. The story holds the man of God to account for disobeying (verses 21-22, 26), while Yahweh's true word later comes through the same man who lied (verse 20).

decisions.choice: an angel: a messenger from God
decisions.reason: The word means "messenger" and is used for a heavenly messenger sent by Yahweh. The old prophet claims a higher source than the man of God's own command.

decisions.choice: a prophet like you: claiming equal standing
decisions.reason: He puts himself on the same level as the man of God, so that his message would carry the same weight.

decisions.choice: But he was lying to him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "But" to show the contrast between the claim and the truth. Readable names the old prophet so the reader knows who lied.

records.source: וַיָּ֣שָׁב אִתּ֗וֹ וַיֹּ֥אכַל לֶ֛חֶם בְּבֵית֖וֹ וַיֵּ֥שְׁתְּ מָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And he returned with him, and ate bread in his house and drank water.
pieces: So the man of God went back with him and ate bread and drank water in his house.

L.19: And he went back with him, and ate bread in his house and drank water.

R.19: So the man of God went back with the old prophet. He ate food and drank water at his house.

decisions.choice: returned, ate, drank: the three things forbidden
decisions.reason: The verbs are the very ones of the command (verses 9, 17). The man of God now does all that he had refused.

decisions.choice: the man of God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject, since two men are in the scene.

records.source: וַיְהִ֕י הֵ֥ם יֹשְׁבִ֖ים אֶל־הַשֻּׁלְחָ֑ןפוַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר־יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־הַנָּבִ֖יא אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֱשִׁיבֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And it was, they [were] sitting at the table, and came [the] word of Yahweh to the prophet who brought him back.
pieces: As they sat at the table, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to the prophet, the very one who had brought him back.

L.20: And it happened, while they [were] sitting at the table, that the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to the prophet who had brought him back.

R.20: While they were sitting at the table, a message from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to the old prophet who had brought the man of God back.

decisions.choice: Yahweh's true word comes through the one who lied
decisions.reason: The prophet who made up a message (verse 18) now receives a real one. The word of Yahweh is not bound to the worthiness of the one who speaks it.

decisions.choice: sitting at the table: sharing the forbidden meal
decisions.reason: The judgment comes in the middle of the very meal the man of God was told not to eat.

decisions.choice: a message from the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable says "message" for "word" here, and names both men.

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֞א אֶל־אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֤א מִֽיהוּדָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה יַ֗עַן כִּ֤י מָרִ֨יתָ֙ פִּ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וְלֹ֤א שָׁמַ֨רְתָּ֙ אֶת־הַמִּצְוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוְּךָ֖ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And he called out to the man of God who came from Judah, saying, Thus says Yahweh: because that you rebelled [against] the mouth of Yahweh and not you kept the command which commanded you Yahweh your God,
pieces: He cried out to the man of God who had come from Judah, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: 'You have defied the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Because you did not keep the command that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God gave you,

L.21: And he called out to the man of God who had come from Judah, saying, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: 'Because you have rebelled against the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and have not kept the command that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God commanded you,

R.21: He shouted to the man of God from Judah, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: 'You have refused to obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You have not kept the command {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God gave you.

decisions.choice: rebelled against the mouth of the LORD: defied what Yahweh said
decisions.reason: "Mouth" stands for what is spoken. The same words are used of Israel's refusal to obey in the wilderness (Numbers 20:24; Deuteronomy 1:26).

decisions.choice: because: the charge comes before the sentence
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on into verse 22: the reason is given first and the penalty at the end.

decisions.choice: the old prophet's words in double quotation marks, the LORD's words in single
decisions.reason: As in verse 2. The quotation runs through verse 22. Literal and Balanced end this verse with a comma because the sentence continues.

records.source: וַתָּ֗שָׁב וַתֹּ֤אכַל לֶ֨חֶם֙ וַתֵּ֣שְׁתְּ מַ֔יִם בַּמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר אֵלֶ֔יךָ אַל־תֹּ֥אכַל לֶ֖חֶם וְאַל־תֵּ֣שְׁתְּ מָ֑יִם לֹֽא־תָב֥וֹא נִבְלָתְךָ֖ אֶל־קֶ֥בֶר אֲבֹתֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: and you returned, and you ate bread and you drank water in the place which he spoke to you, Do not eat bread and do not drink water, not will come your corpse to [the] grave of your fathers.
pieces: and you came back and ate bread and drank water in the very place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told you, "Do not eat bread or drink water," your body will not be buried in the tomb of your ancestors.'"

L.22: and you went back and ate bread and drank water in the place of which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to you, "Do not eat bread and do not drink water," your corpse will not come to the grave of your fathers.'"

R.22: Instead, you came back and ate and drank in the place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told you not to eat or drink. So your body will not be buried in your family's tomb.'"

decisions.choice: the grave of your fathers: burial in the family tomb
decisions.reason: To be buried with one's family mattered greatly (Genesis 47:30; 2 Samuel 19:38). The sentence means he will die away from home and be buried among strangers.

decisions.choice: he spoke to you: Yahweh speaking of himself
decisions.reason: Inside the LORD's message the LORD is spoken of as "he", as often in prophetic speech.

decisions.choice: the three acts of disobedience named
decisions.reason: Returning, eating and drinking are listed one by one, the very acts forbidden in verse 9.

decisions.choice: body (Balanced, Readable); corpse (Literal)
decisions.reason: The word means a dead body. Balanced and Readable say "body" and "buried" for "come to the grave".

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י אַחֲרֵ֛י אָכְל֥וֹ לֶ֖חֶם וְאַחֲרֵ֣י שְׁתוֹת֑וֹ וַיַּחֲבָשׁ־ל֣וֹ הַחֲמ֔וֹר לַנָּבִ֖יא אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֱשִׁיבֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And it was, after his eating bread and after his drinking, and he saddled for him the donkey, for the prophet whom he brought him back.
pieces: After the man of God had eaten bread and drunk, the old prophet saddled the donkey for him, the prophet he had brought back.

L.23: And it happened, after he had eaten bread and after he had drunk, that he saddled the donkey for him, for the prophet whom he had brought back.

R.23: When the man of God had finished eating and drinking, the old prophet saddled a donkey for him. He was the prophet the old man had brought back.

decisions.choice: for the prophet whom he had brought back: the man of God from Judah
decisions.reason: Only here is the man of God called "the prophet". The phrase explains whom the donkey was saddled for: the old prophet gave his guest a donkey for the journey.

decisions.choice: he saddled: the old prophet
decisions.reason: The pronouns in the Hebrew leave the subject open, but the man who brought him back is the host and the one with a donkey to give.

decisions.choice: the man of God; the old prophet
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the two men, since the Hebrew uses only pronouns.

records.source: וַיֵּ֕לֶךְ וַיִּמְצָאֵ֧הוּ אַרְיֵ֛ה בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ וַיְמִיתֵ֑הוּ וַתְּהִ֤י נִבְלָתוֹ֙ מֻשְׁלֶ֣כֶת בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ וְהַחֲמוֹר֙ עֹמֵ֣ד אֶצְלָ֔הּ וְהָ֣אַרְיֵ֔ה עֹמֵ֖ד אֵ֥צֶל הַנְּבֵלָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he went, and found him [a] lion on the way and killed him, and was his corpse thrown in the road, and the donkey [was] standing beside it, and the lion [was] standing beside the corpse.
pieces: He set off, and on the way a lion met him and killed him. His body lay thrown down on the road, with the donkey standing beside it, and the lion standing beside the body too.

L.24: And he went, and a lion met him on the way and killed him; and his corpse was thrown down in the road, and the donkey [was] standing beside it, and the lion [was] standing beside the corpse.

R.24: As the man of God went on his way, a lion attacked him on the road and killed him. His body was left lying on the road. The donkey stood beside it, and the lion stood beside the body too.

decisions.choice: the lion: Yahweh's means of judgment
decisions.reason: The old prophet says so in verse 26: Yahweh gave him to the lion. Lions carry out Yahweh's judgment elsewhere too (20:36; 2 Kings 17:25).

decisions.choice: the lion and the donkey standing side by side
decisions.reason: A lion would normally eat its kill or attack the donkey. That it does neither (verse 28) shows that this was no chance attack.

decisions.choice: corpse: a dead body
decisions.reason: The word is used of a dead body, human or animal, and runs through the rest of the chapter.

decisions.choice: body
decisions.reason: As in verse 22, Balanced and Readable say "body".

records.source: וְהִנֵּ֧ה אֲנָשִׁ֣ים עֹבְרִ֗ים וַיִּרְא֤וּ אֶת־הַנְּבֵלָה֙ מֻשְׁלֶ֣כֶת בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ וְאֶת־הָ֣אַרְיֵ֔ה עֹמֵ֖ד אֵ֣צֶל הַנְּבֵלָ֑ה וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ וַיְדַבְּר֣וּ בָעִ֔יר אֲשֶׁ֛ר הַנָּבִ֥יא הַזָּקֵ֖ן יֹשֵׁ֥ב בָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And look, men passing by, and they saw the corpse thrown in the road, and the lion standing beside the corpse; and they came and spoke in the city which the prophet the old [was] dwelling in it.
pieces: Some men passing by saw the body thrown down on the road and the lion standing beside the body. They went and told about it in the town where the old prophet lived.

L.25: And look, men [were] passing by, and they saw the corpse thrown down in the road and the lion standing beside the corpse; and they came and spoke [of it] in the city where the old prophet was living.

R.25: Some men who were passing by saw the body lying on the road with the lion standing beside it. They went into the town where the old prophet lived and told people what they had seen.

decisions.choice: look: the scene seen through the eyes of the travelers
decisions.reason: The word turns the story to what the passers-by saw.

decisions.choice: the city where the old prophet lived: Bethel
decisions.reason: The town is Bethel (verse 11). The man of God had not got far on his way home.

decisions.choice: told people what they had seen
decisions.reason: Readable says what the men spoke about.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע הַנָּבִיא֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֱשִׁיב֣וֹ מִן־הַדֶּרֶךְ֒ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֣ים ה֔וּא אֲשֶׁ֥ר מָרָ֖ה אֶת־פִּ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּתְּנֵ֨הוּ יְהוָ֜ה לָאַרְיֵ֗ה וַֽיִּשְׁבְּרֵ֨הוּ֙ וַיְמִתֵ֔הוּ כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֶּר־לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And heard the prophet who brought him back from the way, and he said, [The] man of God [is] he who rebelled [against] the mouth of Yahweh; and gave him Yahweh to the lion, and it tore him and killed him according to [the] word of Yahweh which he spoke to him.
pieces: When the prophet who had brought him back from the road heard it, he said, "It is the man of God who defied the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has handed him over to the lion, and it has mauled him and killed him, in keeping with the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke to him."

L.26: And the prophet who had brought him back from the way heard, and he said, "It [is] the man of God who rebelled against the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given him to the lion, and it has torn him and killed him, according to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke to him."

R.26: The old prophet who had brought him back heard about it. He said, "That is the man of God who refused to obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} let the lion attack him and kill him. It happened just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told him it would."

decisions.choice: rebelled against the mouth of the LORD: as in verse 21
decisions.reason: The old prophet repeats the charge of the message he himself had spoken.

decisions.choice: the death is the word of Yahweh fulfilled
decisions.reason: The old prophet reads the lion's attack as the sentence of verses 21-22 carried out. Yahweh's word, given against Bethel's altar and against the disobedient man of God, comes true in both cases.

decisions.choice: tore him: mauled
decisions.reason: The verb means to break or shatter; with a lion it means mauling.

decisions.choice: let the lion attack him
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "gave him to the lion" meant. "According to the word of the LORD" is a different phrase from "by the word of the LORD", so Readable words it differently.

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר אֶל־בָּנָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר חִבְשׁוּ־לִ֖י אֶֽת־הַחֲמ֑וֹר וַֽיַּחֲבֹֽשׁוּ׃
records.gloss: And he spoke to his sons, saying, Saddle for me the donkey; and they saddled.
pieces: Then he said to his sons, "Saddle the donkey for me," and they saddled it.

L.27: And he spoke to his sons, saying, "Saddle the donkey for me." And they saddled [it].

R.27: Then he told his sons, "Get the donkey ready for me to ride," and they saddled it.

decisions.choice: the same order as verse 13
decisions.reason: The words repeat verse 13 almost exactly. The old prophet sets out a second time after the man of God, now to bring back his body.

decisions.choice: Get the donkey ready for me to ride
decisions.reason: As in verse 13.

records.source: וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ וַיִּמְצָ֤א אֶת־נִבְלָתוֹ֙ מֻשְׁלֶ֣כֶת בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ וַֽחֲמוֹר֙ וְהָ֣אַרְיֵ֔ה עֹמְדִ֖ים אֵ֣צֶל הַנְּבֵלָ֑ה לֹֽא־אָכַ֤ל הָֽאַרְיֵה֙ אֶת־הַנְּבֵלָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א שָׁבַ֖ר אֶֽת־הַחֲמֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: And he went and found his corpse thrown in the road, and the donkey and the lion standing beside the corpse; not had eaten the lion the corpse, and not had torn the donkey.
pieces: He went and found the body thrown down on the road, and the donkey and the lion were standing beside it. The lion had neither eaten the body nor mauled the donkey.

L.28: And he went and found his corpse thrown down in the road, and the donkey and the lion standing beside the corpse. The lion had not eaten the corpse and had not torn the donkey.

R.28: He went and found the body lying on the road. The donkey and the lion were standing beside it. The lion had not eaten the body or attacked the donkey.

decisions.choice: the lion held back: a sign that Yahweh was at work
decisions.reason: The lion killed the man and then stood guard. Its strange restraint shows that the death was a judgment, not hunger (see verse 24).

decisions.choice: the body
decisions.reason: As in verse 24.

records.source: וַיִּשָּׂ֨א הַנָּבִ֜יא אֶת־נִבְלַ֧ת אִישׁ־הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים וַיַּנִּחֵ֥הוּ אֶֽל־הַחֲמ֖וֹר וַיְשִׁיבֵ֑הוּ וַיָּבֹ֗א אֶל־עִיר֙ הַנָּבִ֣יא הַזָּקֵ֔ן לִסְפֹּ֖ד וּלְקָבְרֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And lifted the prophet [the] corpse of the man of God and laid it on the donkey and brought it back, and came to [the] city of the prophet the old to mourn and to bury him.
pieces: The prophet lifted the body of the man of God onto the donkey and brought it back. He came into the old prophet's own town to mourn him and bury him.

L.29: And the prophet lifted up the corpse of the man of God and laid it on the donkey and brought it back; and he came to the city of the old prophet to mourn and to bury him.

R.29: The old prophet picked up the body of the man of God, put it on the donkey and brought it back to his own town. He came there to mourn for him and bury him.

decisions.choice: brought it back: the same verb as in verses 18-26
decisions.reason: He had "brought back" the man of God alive, which led to his death; now he brings back his body. The repeated word ties the end of the story to its cause.

decisions.choice: to mourn and to bury: the duty owed to the dead
decisions.reason: Mourning with loud laments and burying the body quickly were the last honors given to the dead (Genesis 23:2-4; 2 Samuel 3:31-32).

decisions.choice: the old prophet's own town; his own town
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names the old prophet again as the owner of the town; Balanced and Readable make clear it is the same man who carries the body.

records.source: וַיַּנַּ֥ח אֶת־נִבְלָת֖וֹ בְּקִבְר֑וֹ וַיִּסְפְּד֥וּ עָלָ֖יו ה֥וֹי אָחִֽי׃
records.gloss: And he laid his corpse in his own grave, and they mourned over him, Alas, my brother!
pieces: He laid the body in his own tomb, and they mourned over him, saying, "Oh, my brother!"

L.30: And he laid his corpse in his own grave, and they mourned over him, "Alas, my brother!"

R.30: He put the body in his own tomb. Then they mourned for him and cried, "Oh, my brother!"

decisions.choice: Alas, my brother: the usual cry of mourning
decisions.reason: The same cry is used for the dead in Jeremiah 22:18. "Brother" here is a word of closeness: the old prophet mourns him as his own.

decisions.choice: his own grave: the old prophet's tomb
decisions.reason: The man of God could not lie in his ancestors' grave (verse 22); he is laid in the tomb the old prophet had prepared for himself.

decisions.choice: they mourned: the old prophet and his household
decisions.reason: The verb is plural; the family and perhaps others of the town joined the lament.

decisions.choice: Oh (Balanced, Readable); Alas (Literal)
decisions.reason: The cry is a sound of grief. Balanced and Readable use "Oh", which sounds natural in modern English.

records.source: וַיְהִי֮ אַחֲרֵ֣י קָבְר֣וֹ אֹתוֹ֒ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֶל־בָּנָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בְּמוֹתִי֙ וּקְבַרְתֶּ֣ם אֹתִ֔י בַּקֶּ֕בֶר אֲשֶׁ֛ר אִ֥ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים קָב֣וּר בּ֑וֹ אֵ֚צֶל עַצְמֹתָ֔יו הַנִּ֖יחוּ אֶת־עַצְמֹתָֽי׃
records.gloss: And it was, after his burying him, and he said to his sons, saying, When I die, and you shall bury me in the grave which the man of God [is] buried in it; beside his bones lay my bones.
pieces: After he had buried him, he said to his sons, "When I die, you are to bury me in the same tomb as the man of God. Put my bones beside his.

L.31: And it happened, after he had buried him, that he spoke to his sons, saying, "When I die, bury me in the grave in which the man of God is buried; lay my bones beside his bones.

R.31: After the burial, the old prophet said to his sons, "When I die, put me in the tomb where the man of God lies. Lay my bones next to his bones.

decisions.choice: my bones beside his bones: kept safe in Josiah's day (2 Kings 23:17-18)
decisions.reason: When Josiah burned bones from the tombs at Bethel, he left this tomb alone because of the man of God from Judah, and the bones of the prophet from Samaria were spared with his (2 Kings 23:17-18).

decisions.choice: buried with the man of God: sharing his honor
decisions.reason: The old prophet believes the prophecy against Bethel will come true (verse 32), and wants his own remains to lie with the one whose word the LORD will honor.

decisions.choice: the speech stays open
decisions.reason: His words continue into verse 32.

records.source: כִּי֩ הָיֹ֨ה יִהְיֶ֜ה הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֤ר קָרָא֙ בִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּבֵֽית־אֵ֑ל וְעַל֙ כָּל־בָּתֵּ֣י הַבָּמ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּעָרֵ֥י שֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃פ
records.gloss: For surely it will happen, the word which he called out by [the] word of Yahweh against the altar which [is] in Bethel, and against all [the] houses of the high places which [are] in [the] cities of Samaria.
pieces: What he cried out by the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will certainly come true, both against the altar in Bethel and against every shrine on the high places in the towns of Samaria."

L.32: For the word that he called out by [the] word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} against the altar that [is] in Bethel, and against all the houses of the high places that [are] in the cities of Samaria, will surely come to pass."

R.32: The message he shouted at {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s command will certainly come true. It was against the altar in Bethel and against all the hilltop shrines in the towns of Samaria."

decisions.choice: the cities of Samaria: the towns of the northern kingdom
decisions.reason: The city of Samaria was built later, by King Omri (16:24), and its name came to be used for the whole northern region (2 Kings 17:24, 26). The narrator uses the name the first readers knew.

decisions.choice: houses of the high places: shrine buildings at the local places of worship
decisions.reason: Jeroboam had built such houses (12:31). The old prophet takes the word against Bethel's altar to cover all the shrines like it, as happened in Josiah's day (2 Kings 23:19).

decisions.choice: surely: the Hebrew doubles the verb for emphasis
decisions.reason: The old prophet, who had lied, is now certain that the man of God's word will come true.

decisions.choice: shrines on the high places (Balanced); hilltop shrines (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Houses" here means shrine buildings. Readable uses its usual wording for the high places.

records.source: אַחַר֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה לֹֽא־שָׁ֥ב יָרָבְעָ֖ם מִדַּרְכּ֣וֹ הָרָעָ֑ה וַ֠יָּשָׁב וַיַּ֜עַשׂ מִקְצ֤וֹת הָעָם֙ כֹּהֲנֵ֣י בָמ֔וֹת הֶֽחָפֵץ֙ יְמַלֵּ֣א אֶת־יָד֔וֹ וִיהִ֖י כֹּהֲנֵ֥י בָמֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: After the matter the this not turned back Jeroboam from his way the evil, and he returned and made from [the] ends of the people priests of high places; the one desiring, he filled his hand, and he became priests of high places.
pieces: Even after this, Jeroboam did not turn from his evil way. Instead he again appointed priests for the high places from all sorts of people. Anyone who wished, he ordained, and that man became one of the priests of the high places.

L.33: After this matter Jeroboam did not turn back from his evil way, but he again made priests of the high places from all the people; whoever desired, he filled his hand, and he became [one of the] priests of the high places.

R.33: Even after all this, Jeroboam did not stop doing evil. Again he chose people from every group to serve as priests at the hilltop shrines. He made anyone who wanted to be a priest into a priest of the shrines.

decisions.choice: did not turn back ... again made: a play on one verb
decisions.reason: The same verb means "turn back" and "do again". Jeroboam did not turn back from his way; instead he turned back to the very thing he had done before (12:31).

decisions.choice: filled his hand: ordained him as priest
decisions.reason: The phrase is the usual way of saying a priest was installed in office (Exodus 28:41; 29:9; Judges 17:5, 12).

decisions.choice: from all the people: not only from the tribe of Levi
decisions.reason: The Law gave the priesthood to Aaron's family of the tribe of Levi (Numbers 3:10). Jeroboam took priests from anywhere (12:31).

decisions.choice: appointed, ordained
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom of the filled hand means.

records.heading: Jeroboam's sin continues

records.source: וַיְהִי֙ בַּדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה לְחַטַּ֖את בֵּ֣ית יָרָבְעָ֑ם וּלְהַכְחִיד֙ וּלְהַשְׁמִ֔יד מֵעַ֖ל פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And it became by the matter the this [the] sin of [the] house of Jeroboam, and to cut [it] off and to destroy [it] from upon [the] face of the ground.
pieces: This became the sin of the house of Jeroboam, and because of it the family was cut off and destroyed from the face of the earth.

L.34: And this matter became the sin of the house of Jeroboam, to cut [it] off and to destroy [it] from the face of the earth.

R.34: This sin brought ruin on Jeroboam's family. Because of it, his whole family was wiped out and removed from the earth.

decisions.choice: this matter became the sin: the practice of making his own priests
alternatives: through this matter sin came to the house of Jeroboam
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "by this matter"; the ancient translations read "this matter" without the small word for "by". Either way the sense is that this practice became the sin of Jeroboam's house.

decisions.choice: cut off and destroyed: fulfilled when Baasha killed Jeroboam's family (15:29-30)
decisions.reason: The prophet Ahijah announces this end in 14:10-11, and 15:29-30 records it.

decisions.choice: the house of Jeroboam: his family and royal line
decisions.reason: "House" means his dynasty, the family that would have ruled after him.

decisions.choice: Jeroboam's family
decisions.reason: Readable says "family" for "house".
